A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-IP research, with matching authors, tasks, and main contributions. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–K support comparison; v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original 20 Questions and MediQ experiments, including model comparisons, predictive accuracy, coverage measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations against probability-calibrated IP in Figure 4.

M1.justification: C-IP retains length-specific conformal thresholds, uniform or direct-prompting history sampling, and greedy prediction-set-size query selection. Appendix G.10 retains the practical stopping procedure. Mathematical corrections, notation changes, and new calibrated-IP comparators do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same AwA2-derived 20-animal task with open/closed queries and binary/free-text answers, plus MediQ's Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, and Neurology categories. The new calibration comparison reuses existing open-query 20Q settings.

E2.justification: v2 adds Platt-scaled IP and temperature-scaled IP as evaluated comparators for open-query 20Q with binary and free-text answers (Figure 4). This substantially extends the comparison to the directly relevant alternative of calibrating probabilities before running IP. The original IP, random selection, direct prompting, and UoT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added calibration experiment introduces per-class logistic regression fitted separately by history length and temperature settings of 0.5, 0.75, and 1.25 (Section 4.2; Appendix G.13). Existing benchmark sample counts, model configurations, accuracy evaluation, and MediQ's three-fold protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds a limited check across temperature-scaling settings. The existing medical walkthrough also changes its displayed query sequence and stopping trace (v1 Figure 5; v2 Figure 6). Appendix F's coverage, estimation-sample-count, and query-count ablations retain their results.

E5.justification: v2's checklist newly states that Sections 4–5 use five runs with different random seeds. v1 already reports five-run means and standard deviations for several 20Q experiments. Both retain three-fold MediQ reporting, whose relationship to the new blanket statement is unexplained. This is additional reporting, not evidence of increased run counts.

E6.justification: New Figure 4 reports C-IP outperforming calibrated IP with binary answers and performing comparably with free-text answers. Section 5.2 replaces the claim of consistently outperforming IP on Internal Medicine and Pediatrics with comparable performance across specialties, while retaining the medical curves. Tables 1–2 and the appendix benchmark and ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (2) corrects an equality between optimal values to an argmax/argmin equivalence, and Remark 1 revises zero-entropy stopping to zero uncertainty reduction. Conversely, v2 Equations (9) and (11) omit lambda_alpha and the factor (1-alpha_N) present in v1's bounds and the retained Proposition 3.1. Dropping these terms preserves query minimizers, but does not justify the stronger displayed inequalities.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: prediction-set-based information pursuit, two history-sampling approaches, and validation on 20Q and MediQ. The added comparisons do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds the hypothesis that complex history distributions explain C-IP's behavior relative to probability-calibration methods. Appendix C's limitations and the existing discussions of calibration failures, instruction-following dependence, and missing sequential risk guarantees remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code-release promise with a repository address and stated availability. Appendix G.13 documents scikit-learn logistic regression, regularization settings, history-length calibration, and temperature choices. G.6 also adds an explicit entropy-estimation formula; this documents the existing estimator rather than establishing an implementation change.

R1.justification: Six references are added, covering calibration methods, scikit-learn, EVINCE, and further IP applications. Sections 2 and B.2–B.3 modestly expand positioning against these works, while retaining the existing related-work organization and principal novelty distinctions.

P1.justification: Sections 2–3 receive localized rewriting and reorganization, including revised history notation, expanded split-conformal explanations, and separate first-query/subsequent-query paragraphs. v2 adds the conference checklist and Appendix G.13, but preserves the abstract, main section sequence, and most appendix prose.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference formatting throughout, changing text width, spacing, and figure sizing. It adds Figure 4, rearranges the medical results from three rows into two rows, redraws the medical walkthrough, and substantially reflows tables, algorithms, and example boxes. These are extensive presentation changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The calibrated-IP comparisons, stated code access, and corrected MediQ performance description improve empirical support and transparency. However, v2's entropy inequalities omit terms required by its retained proposition, and the newly documented entropy estimator in G.6 omits the minus sign. These mathematical regressions counterbalance useful empirical and documentation gains, leaving the overall quality direction unclear.
